intro: Dear members, every week our profession is at work around the world, in foundations and tunnels, slopes and dams, coastlines and cities. Here is a selection of that work, gathered from news sources in many languages and brought to you by the ISSMGE Magazine Presidential Committee.

around_the_world.title: Death toll from mudslides in Nepal rises

case_history.text: On 9 October 1963 about 1,900 to 2,000 people, most of them in Longarone, died when a landslide fell into the Vajont reservoir and sent a wave over the dam. About 400 of them were never found. The slide was an ancient landslide on the north flank of Monte Toc, whose sliding surface followed thin clay layers in the limestone. Filling and drawdown of the new reservoir raised water pressures at its toe, and its creep sped up until about 270 million m³ of rock slid into the reservoir. The dam itself stood. Lesson for practice: Recognise old landslides on reservoir slopes, and assess how filling and drawdown change their stability before and during impounding; slope monitoring is useful only if people act on what it shows.
